name: Euroscepticism
summary: Opposition to, or qualified scepticism about, the European Union and European integration. Hard Euroscepticism rejects the project and wants withdrawal; soft Euroscepticism accepts membership but resists further integration or a federal Europe in the name of national interest and sovereignty. It is held by parties of the right and the left, with right-wing variants adding immigration and identity themes and left-wing ones objecting to neoliberalism and austerity.
scope: Party-based Euroscepticism in the Taggart-Szczerbiak sense, centred on the shared core of sovereignty and anti-federalism, as expressed by Thatcher's Bruges speech, UKIP/Brexit Party, the AfD and similar parties. Because it is a stance on one issue shared by very different parties, most answers outside sovereignty are low-confidence or split; left Euroscepticism (Syriza, Die Linke, Dutch SP) would answer economic statements differently.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; the stance spans parties with opposed views on gender.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between right-wing defence hawks and left-wing anti-militarists.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the democratic-deficit argument: Eurosceptics object to opaque EU decision-making, though the sources do not discuss secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Left Eurosceptics favour capital controls (the Syriza and Die Linke objection to EU free movement of capital), while right-wing and Thatcherite ones oppose them; scope notes this split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the sovereignty emphasis that national authorities should hold the monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: No stated view; inferred from the sovereignty and national-interest emphasis that soldiers should obey national command.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on EU integration shared by right and left parties that split on this.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No documented position; left and right Eurosceptics differ.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Eurosceptics object to EU-imposed fiscal rules but differ on national rules; no common position.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Left Eurosceptics might agree and right ones oppose; the stance does not address it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Eurosceptics seek to reclaim sovereignty through national constitutional channels, as Brexit did, rather than replace the state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Soft Eurosceptic Thatcher-style views favour free markets while left ones favour national economic choice; no shared view.

sacred-nation.rationale: Sovereignty and national identity are core themes, especially in right-wing variants; whether 'sacred' is used varies.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No documented position; adherents divide along left-right lines.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on European integration; adherents are split and no source addresses religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: Left and right Eurosceptics differ on farm policy, and the sources only treat the Common Agricultural Policy as one of many EU grievances.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty core; Thatcher's Bruges speech backed national defence, though adherents across the left and right are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Left Eurosceptics back workers' parties while right ones do not, so adherents are split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; Euroscepticism is an issue stance and its adherents hold no shared view.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split across left and right.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; no shared position among Eurosceptic parties.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; left and right Eurosceptics differ on environmental regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty core: national law is made by national institutions, and no source gives chiefs any role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Adherents are split: some right-wing parties reject green policy while left-wing ones back it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; right-wing variants favour tough sentencing but left-wing ones do not.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Right-wing variants add identity and immigration themes, and the national-sovereignty core favours the national language, though left-wing adherents are less committed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Eurosceptic parties are split: right variants favour voluntary membership, left variants back unions.

voter-id.rationale: The stance is about the EU, and right and left Eurosceptic parties differ on identification at the polls.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Euroscepticism says nothing about the legal status of religious interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the 'democratic deficit' claim, which holds that real popular sovereignty needs national accountability beyond elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Euroscepticism is indifferent to sexual morality, and its right and left variants differ.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the liberty and sovereignty themes of parties like UKIP and the AfD; shutdowns are not a Eurosceptic issue.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; right and left Eurosceptic parties differ on welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: no mainstream Eurosceptic party contests women's equal political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from right-wing variants that defend religion and tradition, while left variants would split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Right-wing variants tend to reject this and left-wing ones accept it, so adherents are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; Eurosceptics split, with some opposing EU-driven gender bodies and others backing national ones.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; Euroscepticism is a stance on integration and its adherents span left and right, so no position can be inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed; sovereignty-minded adherents distrust supranational bodies but many parties of the movement accept the courts, so adherents are split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not addressed; religious conservatives and secular parties both sit within the movement.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; no shared position across the left and right variants.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's centre of gravity in right-wing and national-sovereignty parties (Thatcher, UKIP, AfD), which oppose planned economies; left Eurosceptics would differ.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the movement's complaint that EU decisions are made by remote, unelected bodies and its demand for direct national democratic accountability.

national-church-status.rationale: Not addressed; right-wing strands often favour national churches while left strands do not, so adherents are split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; some parties favour regional autonomy and others stress a unitary nation-state, so adherents are split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reliance on referendums, such as the 2016 UK vote, and its appeal to the people's right to decide.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no position on post-colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; unrelated to the integration issue.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; right-wing strands stress immigration limits generally but have no position on indigenous regions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views on conscription and sex equality.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: National-sovereignty variants stress attachment to the nation and its land, but the shared core is only the EU stance, so adherents differ; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Euroscepticism says nothing on drug policy; the right-wing variants lean tough but most parties support due process; inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: Adherents are split: some right Eurosceptics favour trade with China, others and left variants are hostile; no source treats it as part of the stance.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Some right-wing parties champion kin abroad (Hungary), while others do not; the stance itself does not address it.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Left and right Eurosceptics split on resource ownership; the stance is not about it.

self-ownership.rationale: The stance is about European integration, and adherents on left and right differ on individual rights over property and labour.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Adherents are split by left and right economics, and no source ties consumption taxes to it.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Left variants favour universal welfare while right variants favour targeting; split.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Populist Eurosceptics criticise elites and intermediaries, but the scholarship ties this only to part of the stance and many parties are conventional.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Both anti-elite right and left Eurosceptics criticise crony business, but the stance is not about it; split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The stance is not about religion and adherents range from Christian conservatives to secular leftists.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; right-wing variants appeal to tradition, left variants do not.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Adherents are split between socially conservative and liberal parties.

national-resource-control.rationale: Sovereignty is the shared core, and the Bruges speech and AfD programme object to Brussels control; resource control is inferred from that sovereignty theme.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Euroscepticism is a stance on integration spanning left and right, so adherents are split and no source addresses it.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Eurosceptic parties are split, with some left parties favouring it and many right parties opposing an EU-level tax; none of the sources address it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not part of the shared core; right-wing Eurosceptic parties lean agree and left ones disagree, so adherents are split.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not part of the shared core; inferred, with no source addressing it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not part of the shared core and no source addresses it; adherents are split.

multipolar-world.rationale: The sovereignty core and the AfD's call for a Europe of fatherlands fit several independent centres of power, but the sources do not address world order directly.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Left Eurosceptics might accept it and right ones reject it; the sources do not address it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Eurosceptic parties often join national pride with appeals to ordinary people against elites, but this is inferred and varies between left and right.

material-over-identity.rationale: Left Eurosceptics would agree and right-wing ones stress identity, so adherents are split; no source addresses it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Eurosceptic parties work within multiparty democracy and do not seek communist party rule, though left Eurosceptics differ; inferred.

notes: Euroscepticism is defined by one issue, so the profile is thin outside sovereignty and integration. Strands differ: right-wing parties add immigration and identity; left-wing ones object to neoliberalism and austerity; the Brexit era blurred hard and soft by shifting from exit to reform (per ECPS). Primary sources could not be opened in full (margaretthatcher.org blocked), so the Bruges text is taken from quoted passages.
